--------
Dale Comstock sits down with Vlad to recount a harrowing 1990 mission in Panama’s remote Darién jungle, months after the Modelo Prison rescue involving Kurt Muse. Comstock describes how an overloaded Black Hawk carrying soldiers, equipment, and a 400-gallon auxiliary fuel tank lost its left engine mid-flight, struck trees, snapped its rotor blades, and plunged 206 feet like a “lawn dart.”  

The crash left five men with broken backs, including Comstock, and two soldiers paralyzed—among them his assistant team leader, who had already survived a rotor strike during the earlier Kurt Muse rescue. Comstock reflects on survival, physical conditioning, the dangers of military aviation, Panamanian Defense Forces holdouts, and the sacrifices made by disabled veterans who rarely receive public recognition.  

A gripping firsthand account of special operations, jungle training, Black Hawk crashes, and the lasting cost of service.

--------
Ramon “Mundo” Mendoza sits down with Vlad to revisit *American Me*, the Edward James Olmos film that shaped public perceptions of prison life, gang politics, and the Mexican Mafia. Vlad explains how one disturbing prison scene became a personal deterrent, while Mendoza discusses Olmos’ acting legacy in *Stand and Deliver*, *Blade Runner*, and *Miami Vice* while questioning how accurately the movie depicted gang culture.

The conversation turns to the film’s storyline involving Santana, Puppet, and the order to kill a younger brother. Mendoza says that exact scenario was fictionalized, but recalls a real San Fernando Valley case from Sylmar involving brothers connected to Mexican Mafia politics, alleged extortion, territorial disputes, and a hit carried out in the late 1970s. He also references his book *Gang of Gangs* while separating Hollywood dramatization from real prison history.
